newsitem.title: USA: India sovereign rating outlook unfavorable - Moody's.
newsitem.headline: India sovereign rating outlook unfavorable - Moody's.

text.p: India's unstable political environment, directionless economic policies, and a deterioration in its macroeconomic balances have led Moody's Investors Service Inc to take an unfavorable outlook on the nation's Baa3 sovereign rating, the agency said.
Moody's, which upgraded India's rating from Ba2 to Baa3 in December, 1994, recently assessed potential pressure on the rating over an 18- to 24-month horizon.

Its report said India's growth is hindered by inadequate infrastructure, while domestic savings is incapable of providing sufficient capital for needed development. At the same time, the current governmental policy does not foster a favorable environment for external financing, said Moody's sovereign ratings analyst Kristin Lindow.
A sluggish pace of industrial production and a "disturbing" drop in export growth were responsible for slowing economic growth, Moody's said, portending a worsened financial condition.

"The slowdown, coupled with virtually no sale of state assets, suggests that the budget deficit will be above target," Moody's said, adding that a higher oil bill could mean that trade and current accounts may not improve as growth decelerates.
India has also been beset with an increasingly large current account deficit and the loss of reserves over the past two years, Lindow said.

"Reserve coverage has dropped from over six months to under four months of imports," she said. "That's a concern because in a big country like (India) which has had balance of payments pressures arise before, we know that imports tend to be underestimated concurrently and that means they may be in even a more fragile situation."

Further, the rating agency said India's political framework is "unwieldy" due to the multi-party coalition government that is supported by a Congress party weakened by corruption scandals and a leadership vacuum.
Inflation in India is low, but is on an upward track, Moody's said.
